title: Talking Plant Cutouts for Blind Classmates
title_te: చూపు లేని సహవిద్యార్థుల కోసం మాట్లాడే మొక్క కటౌట్లు
problem: In science class, blind students touch textbook diagrams but cannot understand which part is the stem, root, or leaf without constant help.
idea: Cardboard plant parts that talk. When a classmate shows a cutout to the camera, the computer says what it is and what it does. Here you can tap the cutout the camera 'sees'.

widgets.heading: 🎯 Try it: Which cutout is shown?
widgets.intro: In my real project, Teachable Machine learns each cardboard shape. Here, tap a cutout.
widgets.question: My classmate holds up:

options.label: Thin branching pieces
options.result: This is the ROOT. It holds the plant in the soil and drinks water.
options.te: ఇది వేరు. మొక్కను నేలలో పట్టుకుని నీరు పీల్చుకుంటుంది.

options.label: Long straight stick
options.result: This is the STEM. It holds the plant up and carries water to the leaves.
options.te: ఇది కాండం. మొక్కను నిలబెట్టి ఆకులకు నీరు పంపుతుంది.

options.label: Flat shape with lines
options.result: This is the LEAF. It makes food using sunlight.
options.te: ఇది ఆకు. సూర్యకాంతితో ఆహారం తయారు చేస్తుంది.

options.label: Round shape with petals
options.result: This is the FLOWER. It makes seeds and fruits.
options.te: ఇది పువ్వు. విత్తనాలు, పండ్లు తయారు చేస్తుంది.

questions.q: Which part drinks water from the soil?
questions.why: Roots take water and minerals from the soil.

questions.q: Which part makes food for the plant?
questions.why: Leaves make food using sunlight. This is photosynthesis.

questions.q: Which part carries water up to the leaves?
questions.why: The stem is like a pipe that carries water up.

questions.q: Why do we make the cutouts with different textures?
options: So blind friends can feel the difference
questions.why: Rough, smooth and bumpy textures help friends identify parts by touch.

how: Cut root, stem, leaf and flower shapes from cardboard. Stick thread, sandpaper or cloth so each feels different.
Open Teachable Machine, choose Image Project, and make one class per part plus 'Nothing'.
Show each cutout to the webcam from many angles to take about 50 photos each.
Train, Export and load the model in Scratch.
Ask Gemini for one simple sentence about each part, and add it to a Text-to-Speech block.
Let blind classmates try it and ask them how to make it better.
prompt: I am a Class 8 student. Write one short sentence in simple English and Telugu explaining each plant part (root, stem, leaf, flower, fruit) for a blind classmate who is touching a cardboard model.
